newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end down two pct, weary of Wall St.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end down two pct, weary of Wall St.

text.p: French shares finished with another sizeable loss on Wednesday, after an attempt to retrace Tuesday's 2.82 percent drop ran out of momentum.

Traders said it was hard to call the market's direction as prices were highly sensitive to gyrations on Wall Street. "It's easier to watch which way the market's going and then go with the flow," said one trader.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 51.54 points or 2.0 percent at 2,530.20. The CAC-40 futures contract was down 50 points at 2,527 from Tuesday's close.

The CAC index breached a major support level at 2,550, falling on worries over further U.S. interest rate rises. There was caution ahead of Friday's U.S. unemployment figures, with a market consensus of a 5.2 percent rise for March.

* Suez lost 1.15 percent to 282.60 francs. Yield funds were disappointed Suez was apparently capping its dividend, which includes a special payout on its Banque Indosuez sale, at around 20 francs per share instead of the more than 30 francs for which the market was hoping.
* Lyonnaise des Eaux shed 2.89 percent to 538, as speculation burst. The planned merger is fully priced in.
* Alcatel Alsthom bucks the market, rising 0.74 percent to 678. One trader said U.S. funds seemed to have revalued the stock following last week's news that U.S. giant Fidelity had raised its stake.

* Lagardere closed down 0.45 percent at 178.10. It reported a 1996 net attributable profit of 1.04 billion francs and said it was aware that Britain's GEC Plc was bidding for defence electronic firm Thomson-CSF.
* Generale des Eaux, down 1.2 percent at 741, reports 1996 results on Thursday. The company has previously forecast a net attributable profit of 1.8 billion francs.
